<content>
1: # Coral NPU
2: 
3: Coral NPU is a hardware accelerator for ML inferencing. Coral NPU is an Open Source IP designed by Google Research and is freely available for integration into ultra-low-power System-on-Chips (SoCs) targeting wearable devices such as hearables, augmented reality (AR) glasses and smart watches.
4: 
5: Coral NPU is a neural processing unit (NPU), also known as an AI accelerator or deep-learning processor. Coral NPU is based on the 32-bit RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture (ISA).
6: 
7: Coral NPU includes three distinct processor components that work together: matrix, vector (SIMD), and scalar.
8: 
9: ![Coral NPU Archicture](doc/images/arch_data_flow.png)
10: [Coral NPU Architecture Datasheet](https://developers.google.com/coral/guides/hardware/datasheet)
11: 
12: ## Coral NPU Features
13: Coral NPU offers the following top-level feature set:
14: 
15: * RV32IMF_Zve32x RISC-V instruction set (specifically `rv32imf_zve32x_zicsr_zifencei_zbb`)
16: * 32-bit address space for applications and operating system kernels
17: * Four-stage processor, in-order dispatch, out-of-order retire
18: * Four-way scalar, two-way vector dispatch
19: * 128-bit SIMD, 256-bit (future) pipeline
20: * 8 KB ITCM memory (tightly-coupled memory for instructions)
21: * 32 KB DTCM memory (tightly-coupled memory for data)
22: * Both memories are single-cycle-latency SRAM, more efficient than cache memory
23: * AXI4 bus interfaces, functioning as both manager and subordinate, to interact with external memory and allow external CPUs to configure Coral NPU
24: 
25: ## System Requirements
26: 
27: * Bazel 7.4.1
28: * Python 3.9-3.12 (3.13 support is in progress)
29: * [SRecord](https://srecord.sourceforge.net/)
30: 
31: ## Quick Start
32: 
33: ```bash
34: # Ensure that test suite passes
35: bazel run //tests/cocotb:core_mini_axi_sim_cocotb
36: 
37: # Build a binary
38: bazel build //examples:coralnpu_v2_hello_world_add_floats
39: 
40: # Build the Simulator (non-RVV for shorter build time):
41: bazel build //tests/verilator_sim:core_mini_axi_sim
42: 
43: # Run the binary on the simulator:
44: bazel-bin/tests/verilator_sim/core_mini_axi_sim --binary bazel-out/k8-fastbuild-ST-dd8dc713f32d/bin/examples/coralnpu_v2_hello_world_add_floats.elf
45: ```
46: 
47: 
48: ![](doc/images/Coral_Logo_200px-2x.png)

(End of file - total 48 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: # CoralNPU
2: 
3: CoralNPU is a RISCV CPU built with custom SIMD instructions and microarchitectural
4: decisions that align with the dataplane properties of an ML accelerator. The design
5: of CoralNPU starts with domain and matrix capabilities; vector and scalar
6: capabilities are then added for a fused design.
7: 
8: ## Block Diagram
9: 
10: ![CoralNPU block diagram](images/coralnpu_block.png)
11: 
12: ## Scalar Core
13: 
14: A simple RISC-V scalar frontend drives the command queues of the ML+SIMD
15: backend.
16: 
17: CoralNPU utilizes a custom RISC-V frontend (rv32im) that runs the minimal set of
18: instructions to support an executor run-to-completion model (eg. no OS, no
19: interrupts), with all control tasks onloaded to the SMC . The C extension
20: encoding is reclaimed (as per the risc-v specification) to provide the necessary
21: encoding space for the SIMD registers (6b indices), and to allow flexible type
22: encodings and instruction compression (stripmining) for the SIMD instruction
23: set. The scalar core is an in order machine with no speculation.
24: 
25: The branch policy in the fetch stage is backwards branches are taken and forward
26: branches are not-taken, incurring a penalty cycle if the execute result does not
27: match the decision in the fetch unit.
28: 
29: Registers        | Names         | Width
30: ---------------- | ------------- | -----------------------
31: Scalar (31)      | zero, x1..x31 | 32 bits
32: Control & Status | CSRx          | Various
33: 
34: ## Vector Core
35: 
36: We use SIMD and vector interchangeably, referring to a simple and practical SIMD
37: instruction definition devoid of variable length behaviors. The scalar frontend
38: is decoupled from the backend by a FIFO structure that buffers vector
39: instructions, posting only to the relevant command queues when dependencies are
40: resolved in the vector regfile. The vector core supports data widths of 8, 16, and 32 bits.
41: 
42: Registers        | Names         | Width
43: ---------------- | ------------- | -----------------------
44: Vector (64)      | v0..v63       | 256 bits (eg. int32 x8)
45: Accumulator      | acc<8><8>     | 8x8x 32 bits
46: 
47: 
48: ### MAC
49: 
50: The central component of the design is a quantized outer product
51: multiply-accumulate engine. An outer-product engine provides two-dimensional
52: broadcast structures to maximize the amount of deliverable compute with respect
53: to memory accesses. On one axis is a parallel broadcast (“wide”, convolution
54: weights), and the other axis the transpose shifted inputs of a number of batches
55: (“narrow”, eg. MobileNet XY batching).
56: 
57: ![CoralNPU MAC](images/coralnpu_aconv.png)
58: 
59: The outer-product construction is a vertical arrangement of multiple VDOT
60: opcodes which utilize 4x 8bit multiplies reduced into 32 bit accumulators and
61: performing 256 MACs per cycle.
62: 
63: ### Stripmining
64: 
65: Strip mining is defined as folding array-based parallelism to fit the available
66: hardware parallelism. To reduce frontend instruction dispatch pressure becoming
67: a bottleneck, and to natively support instruction level tiling patterns through
68: the SIMD registers, the instruction encoding shall explicitly include a
69: stripmine mechanism that converts a single frontend dispatch event to the
70: command queue into four serialized issue events into the SIMD units. For
71: instance a “vadd v0” in Dispatch will produce “vadd v0 : vadd v1 : vadd v2 :
72: vadd v3” at Issue. These will be processed as four discrete events.
73: 
74: ## Cache
75: 
76: Caches exists as a single layer between the core and the first level of shared
77: SRAM. The L1 cache and scalar core frontend are an overhead to the rest of the
78: backend compute pipeline and ideally are as small as possible.
79: 
80: The L1Icache is 8KB (256b blocks * 256 slots) with 4-way set associativity.
81: 
82: The L1Dcache sizing is towards the scalar core requirements to perform loop
83: management and address generation. The L1Dcache is 16KB (SIMD256b) with low set
84: associativity of 4-way. The L1Dcache is implemented with a dual bank
85: architecture where each bank is 8KB (similar to L1Icache). This property allows
86: for a degree of next line prefetch. The L1Dcache also serves as an alignment
87: buffer for the scalar and SIMD instructions to assist development and to
88: simplify software support. In an embedded setting, the L1Dcache provides half of
89: the memory bandwidth to the ML outer-product engine when only a single external
90: memory port is provided. Line and all entry flushing is supported where the core
91: stalls until completion to simplify the contract.

(End of file - total 91 lines)

12: trait WithVcd { this: HasCliOptions =>
13:   override implicit def backendSettingsModifications: svsim.BackendSettingsModifications =
14:     (original: svsim.Backend.Settings) => {
15:       original match {
16:         case settings: Backend.CompilationSettings =>
17:           settings.copy(
18:             traceStyle = Some(
19:               Backend.CompilationSettings.TraceStyle.Vcd(filename = "trace.vcd")
20:             )
21:           )
22:         case other => other
23:       }
24:     }
25: 
26:   override implicit def commonSettingsModifications: svsim.CommonSettingsModifications =
27:     (original: CommonCompilationSettings) => {
28:       original.copy(
29:         simulationSettings = original.simulationSettings.copy(enableWavesAtTimeZero = true)
30:       )
31:     }
32: }

34: class AsyncQueueSmokeTest extends Module {
35:   val io = IO(new Bundle {
36:     val enq = Flipped(Decoupled(UInt(32.W)))
37:     val deq = Decoupled(UInt(32.W))
38:   })
39: 
40:   // Create two asynchronous clock sources from the single test clock
41:   val enq_clock_wire = Wire(Clock())
42:   val deq_clock_wire = Wire(Clock())
43:   val enq_reset_wire = Wire(Bool())
44:   val deq_reset_wire = Wire(Bool())
45: 
46:   // A simple clock divider to create a slower enqueue clock (half frequency).
47:   val enq_clock_divider = RegInit(false.B)
48:   enq_clock_divider := !enq_clock_divider
49:   enq_clock_wire := enq_clock_divider.asClock
50: 
51:   // A different divider to create an even slower dequeue clock (quarter frequency)
52:   // that is phase-shifted relative to the enqueue clock.
53:   val deq_clock_divider = RegInit(0.U(2.W))
54:   deq_clock_divider := deq_clock_divider + 1.U
55:   deq_clock_wire := deq_clock_divider(1).asClock
56: 
57:   // Tie resets to the main test harness reset
58:   enq_reset_wire := reset.asBool
59:   deq_reset_wire := reset.asBool
60: 
61:   // safe=false is used for performance in this simple test. For production,
62:   // safe=true is recommended to prevent metastability issues when the queue
63:   // is nearly full or empty.
64:   val queue = Module(new AsyncQueue(UInt(32.W), AsyncQueueParams.singleton(safe = false)))
65: 
66:   queue.io.enq_clock := enq_clock_wire
67:   queue.io.enq_reset := enq_reset_wire
68:   queue.io.deq_clock := deq_clock_wire
69:   queue.io.deq_reset := deq_reset_wire
70: 
71:   queue.io.enq <> io.enq
72:   io.deq <> queue.io.deq
73: }
74: 
75: class AsyncQueueSmokeSpec extends AnyFreeSpec with ChiselSim with WithVcd {
76:   "AsyncQueueSmokeTest should pass a value across clock domains" in {
77:     simulate(new AsyncQueueSmokeTest) { dut =>
78:       val resetCycles = 2
79:       val initialDelayCycles = 5
80:       val enqHoldCycles = 3
81:       val deqValidTimeoutCycles = 50
82: 
83:       // Initialize inputs
84:       dut.io.enq.valid.poke(false.B)
85:       dut.io.deq.ready.poke(false.B)
86: 
87:       // Reset the DUT
88:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
89:       dut.clock.step(resetCycles)
90:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
91:       dut.clock.step(initialDelayCycles)
92: 
93:       // Enqueue an item
94:       dut.io.enq.valid.poke(true.B)
95:       dut.io.enq.bits.poke(123.U)
96:       dut.io.enq.ready.expect(true.B) // Should be ready immediately after reset
97:       // Hold valid for enough cycles to guarantee a rising edge on the slower enq_clock
98:       dut.clock.step(enqHoldCycles)
99:       dut.io.enq.valid.poke(false.B)
100: 
101:       // Wait for deq.valid to go high, with a timeout
102:       var timeout = deqValidTimeoutCycles
103:       while (!dut.io.deq.valid.peek().litToBoolean && timeout > 0) {
104:         dut.clock.step()
105:         timeout -= 1
106:       }
107:       if (timeout == 0) {
108:         fail(s"Timed out after ${deqValidTimeoutCycles} cycles waiting for deq.valid to go high")
109:       }
110: 
111:       // Dequeue the item
112:       dut.io.deq.ready.poke(true.B)
113:       dut.io.deq.valid.expect(true.B)
114:       dut.io.deq.bits.expect(123.U)
115:       dut.clock.step()
116:     }
117:   }
118: }

package common

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._

class Fp32 extends Bundle {
  val sign = Bool()
  val exponent = UInt(8.W)
  val mantissa = UInt(23.W)

  def isZero(): Bool = exponent === 0.U && mantissa === 0.U
  def isInf(): Bool = exponent === 255.U && mantissa === 0.U
  def isNan(): Bool = exponent === 255.U && mantissa =/= 0.U

  def asUInt32(): UInt = {
    Cat(sign, exponent, mantissa)
  }
}

object Fp32 {
  def apply(): Fp32 = new Fp32

  def fromWord(word: UInt): Fp32 = {
    val fp = Wire(new Fp32)
    fp.sign := word(31)
    fp.exponent := word(30, 23)
    fp.mantissa := word(22, 0)
    fp
  }

  def fromInteger(int: UInt, isSigned: Bool): Fp32 = {
    val fp = Wire(new Fp32)
    val absInt = Mux(isSigned && int(31), (~int).asUInt + 1.U, int)
    val sign = isSigned && int(31)

    // Find leading zero count
    val lz = Wire(UInt(6.W))
    lz := PriorityEncoder(Reverse(absInt))

    val width = 32.U - lz
    val normalized = Mux(width === 0.U, 0.U, (absInt << lz)(30, 8))
    val exponent = Mux(width === 0.U, 0.U, width + 126.U)

    fp.sign := sign
    fp.exponent := exponent(7, 0)
    fp.mantissa := normalized(22, 0)
    fp
  }
}

class FmaCmd extends Bundle {
  val ina = new Fp32
  val inb = new Fp32
  val inc = new Fp32
}

class FmaState1 extends Bundle {
  val sign = Bool()
  val exp = UInt(10.W)
  val mant = UInt(48.W)
  val cSign = Bool()
  val cExp = UInt(10.W)
  val cMant = UInt(48.W)
  val isZero = Bool()
  val isInf = Bool()
  val isNan = Bool()
}

class FmaState2 extends Bundle {
  val sign = Bool()
  val exp = UInt(10.W)
  val mant = UInt(48.W)
  val isZero = Bool()
  val isInf = Bool()
  val isNan = Bool()
}

object Fma {
  def FmaStage1(cmd: FmaCmd): FmaState1 = {
    val s1 = Wire(new FmaState1)

    val aIsZero = cmd.ina.isZero()
    val bIsZero = cmd.inb.isZero()
    val cIsZero = cmd.inc.isZero()
    val aIsInf = cmd.ina.isInf()
    val bIsInf = cmd.inb.isInf()
    val cIsInf = cmd.inc.isInf()
    val aIsNan = cmd.ina.isNan()
    val bIsNan = cmd.inb.isNan()
    val cIsNan = cmd.inc.isNan()

    val mulSign = cmd.ina.sign ^ cmd.inb.sign
    val mulExp = (cmd.ina.exponent + cmd.inb.exponent).asUInt - 127.U
    val aMant = Mux(aIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.ina.mantissa))
    val bMant = Mux(bIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.inb.mantissa))
    val mulMant = (aMant.asUInt * bMant.asUInt)(47, 0)

    val cMant = Mux(cIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.inc.mantissa))

    s1.sign := mulSign
    s1.exp := mulExp
    s1.mant := mulMant
    s1.cSign := cmd.inc.sign
    s1.cExp := cmd.inc.exponent
    s1.cMant := Cat(cMant, 0.U(24.W))
    s1.isZero := aIsZero || bIsZero
    s1.isInf := aIsInf || bIsInf
    s1.isNan := aIsNan || bIsNan || cIsNan || ((aIsInf && bIsZero) || (aIsZero && bIsInf))

    s1
  }

  def FmaStage2(s1: FmaState1): FmaState2 = {
    val s2 = Wire(new FmaState2)

    val cIsZero = s1.cExp === 0.U && s1.cMant === 0.U
    val expDiff = s1.exp.asSInt - s1.cExp.asSInt
    val alignedCMant = Mux(expDiff >= 0.S, s1.cMant >> expDiff.asUInt, s1.cMant << (-expDiff).asUInt)

    val addMant = Mux(s1.sign === s1.cSign, s1.mant + alignedCMant, s1.mant - alignedCMant)
    val subMant = Mux(s1.sign === s1.cSign, s1.mant - alignedCMant, s1.mant + alignedCMant)

    val resultSign = Mux(addMant(48), s1.sign, s1.cSign)
    val resultMant = Mux(addMant(48), addMant, subMant)
    val resultExp = Mux(addMant(48), s1.exp, s1.cExp)

    val lz = PriorityEncoder(Reverse(resultMant))
    val normalizedMant = (resultMant << lz)(47, 0)
    val normalizedExp = resultExp - lz

    s2.sign := resultSign
    s2.exp := Mux(cIsZero, s1.exp, normalizedExp)
    s2.mant := Mux(cIsZero, s1.mant, normalizedMant)
    s2.isZero := s1.isZero && cIsZero
    s2.isInf := s1.isInf || s1.cExp === 255.U
    s2.isNan := s1.isNan || (s1.isInf && s1.cExp === 255.U && s1.sign =/= s1.cSign)

    s2
  }

  def FmaStage3(s2: FmaState2): Fp32 = {
    val out = Wire(new Fp32)

    val lz = PriorityEncoder(Reverse(s2.mant))
    val normalized = (s2.mant << lz)(47, 0)
    val newExp = s2.exp - lz + 1.U

    val guardBit = normalized(23)
    val roundBit = normalized(22)
    val stickyBit = normalized(21, 0).orR
    val roundUp = guardBit && (roundBit || stickyBit || normalized(24))

    val roundedMant = normalized(46, 24) + Mux(roundUp, 1.U, 0.U)
    val finalExp = newExp + Mux(roundUp && roundedMant === 0.U, 1.U, 0.U)

    val overflow = finalExp >= 255.U
    val underflow = finalExp === 0.U || s2.mant === 0.U

    out.sign := s2.sign
    out.exponent := MuxCase(finalExp, Seq(
      s2.isNan -> 255.U,
      s2.isInf -> 255.U,
      overflow -> 255.U,
      underflow -> 0.U
    ))
    out.mantissa := MuxCase(roundedMant(22, 0), Seq(
      s2.isNan -> 1.U,
      s2.isInf -> 0.U,
      overflow -> 0.U,
      underflow -> 0.U,
      s2.isZero -> 0.U
    ))

    out
  }
}

package common

import chisel3._
import chisel3.util._

class FmaCmd extends Bundle {
  val ina = new Fp32
  val inb = new Fp32
  val inc = new Fp32
}

class FmaState1 extends Bundle {
  val sign = Bool()
  val exp = SInt(10.W)
  val mant = UInt(48.W)
  val cSign = Bool()
  val cExp = SInt(10.W)
  val cMant = UInt(48.W)
  val isZero = Bool()
  val isInf = Bool()
  val isNan = Bool()
}

class FmaState2 extends Bundle {
  val sign = Bool()
  val exp = SInt(10.W)
  val mant = UInt(48.W)
  val isZero = Bool()
  val isInf = Bool()
  val isNan = Bool()
}

object Fma {
  def FmaStage1(cmd: FmaCmd): FmaState1 = {
    val s1 = Wire(new FmaState1)

    val aIsZero = cmd.ina.isZero()
    val bIsZero = cmd.inb.isZero()
    val cIsZero = cmd.inc.isZero()
    val aIsInf = cmd.ina.isInf()
    val bIsInf = cmd.inb.isInf()
    val cIsInf = cmd.inc.isInf()
    val aIsNan = cmd.ina.isNan()
    val bIsNan = cmd.inb.isNan()
    val cIsNan = cmd.inc.isNan()

    val mulSign = cmd.ina.sign ^ cmd.inb.sign
    val mulExp = (cmd.ina.exponent.zext +& cmd.inb.exponent.zext) - 127.S
    val aMant = Mux(aIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.ina.mantissa))
    val bMant = Mux(bIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.inb.mantissa))
    val mulMant = (aMant.asUInt * bMant.asUInt)(47, 0)

    val cMantRaw = Mux(cIsZero, 0.U(24.W), Cat(1.U(1.W), cmd.inc.mantissa))
    val cMant48 = (cMantRaw << 23).asUInt

    s1.sign := mulSign
    s1.exp := mulExp
    s1.mant := mulMant
    s1.cSign := cmd.inc.sign
    s1.cExp := cmd.inc.exponent.zext
    s1.cMant := cMant48
    s1.isZero := aIsZero || bIsZero
    s1.isInf := aIsInf || bIsInf
    s1.isNan := aIsNan || bIsNan || cIsNan || ((aIsInf && bIsZero) || (aIsZero && bIsInf))

    s1
  }

  def FmaStage2(s1: FmaState1): FmaState2 = {
    val s2 = Wire(new FmaState2)

    val cIsZero = s1.cExp === 0.S && s1.cMant === 0.U
    val cIsInf = s1.cExp === 255.S && s1.cMant === 0.U

    val expDiff = s1.exp - s1.cExp
    val abMant = s1.mant
    val cMant48 = s1.cMant

    val alignedAB = Wire(UInt(48.W))
    val alignedC = Wire(UInt(48.W))
    val resultExp = Wire(SInt(10.W))

    when(expDiff >= 0.S) {
      alignedAB := abMant
      alignedC := (cMant48 >> expDiff.asUInt).asUInt
      resultExp := s1.exp
    }.otherwise {
      alignedAB := (abMant >> (-expDiff).asUInt).asUInt
      alignedC := cMant48
      resultExp := s1.cExp
    }

    val resultMant = Wire(UInt(48.W))
    val resultSign = Wire(Bool())

    when(s1.sign === s1.cSign) {
      resultMant := alignedAB + alignedC
      resultSign := s1.sign
    }.otherwise {
      when(alignedAB >= alignedC) {
        resultMant := alignedAB - alignedC
        resultSign := s1.sign
      }.otherwise {
        resultMant := alignedC - alignedAB
        resultSign := s1.cSign
      }
    }

    s2.sign := resultSign
    s2.exp := resultExp
    s2.mant := resultMant
    s2.isZero := (s1.isZero && cIsZero) || (resultMant === 0.U && !s1.isNan && !s1.isInf && !cIsInf)
    s2.isInf := (s1.isInf && !cIsInf) || (cIsInf && !s1.isInf) || (s1.isInf && cIsInf && s1.sign === s1.cSign)
    s2.isNan := s1.isNan || (s1.isInf && cIsInf && s1.sign =/= s1.cSign)

    s2
  }

  def FmaStage3(s2: FmaState2): Fp32 = {
    val out = Wire(new Fp32)

    val lz = PriorityEncoder(Reverse(s2.mant))
    val normalized = (s2.mant << lz).asUInt
    val newExp = s2.exp - lz.zext + 1.S

    val guardBit = normalized(23)
    val roundBit = normalized(22)
    val stickyBit = normalized(21, 0).orR
    val roundUp = guardBit && (roundBit || stickyBit)

    val mantissaRaw = normalized(46, 24)
    val roundedMant = mantissaRaw + Mux(roundUp, 1.U, 0.U)
    val mantissaOverflow = roundedMant(23)
    val finalMant = Mux(mantissaOverflow, roundedMant(22, 0), roundedMant(22, 0))
    val finalExp = Mux(mantissaOverflow, newExp + 1.S, newExp)

    val overflow = finalExp >= 255.S
    val underflow = finalExp <= 0.S || s2.mant === 0.U

    out.sign := s2.sign
    out.exponent := MuxCase(finalExp.asUInt(7, 0), Seq(
      s2.isNan -> 255.U,
      s2.isInf -> 255.U,
      overflow -> 255.U,
      underflow -> 0.U,
      s2.isZero -> 0.U
    ))
    out.mantissa := MuxCase(finalMant, Seq(
      s2.isNan -> 1.U,
      s2.isInf -> 0.U,
      overflow -> 0.U,
      underflow -> 0.U,
      s2.isZero -> 0.U
    ))

    out
  }
}

22: /** Test suite for SPI Master implementation.
23:   *
24:   * Covers register access, data path (loopback), baud rate timing, manual chip-select control, and
25:   * asynchronous clock domain crossing.
26:   */
27: class SpiMasterSpec extends AnyFreeSpec with ChiselSim with TLULTestUtils {
28:   val p = new Parameters
29: 
30:   "SpiMaster Register Access" in {
31:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
32:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
33:       dut.clock.step()
34:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
35: 
36:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x1234.U) // CONTROL
37:       val rdata = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U)
38:       assert(rdata == 0x1234)
39:     }
40:   }
41: 
42:   "SpiMaster Loopback" in {
43:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
44:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
45:       dut.clock.step()
46:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
47: 
48:       // Enable SPI
49:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x01.U) // ENABLE=1
50:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, 0x55.U) // TXDATA=0x55
51: 
52:       // Sample MOSI and feed back to MISO to simulate wire loopback
53:       for (_ <- 0 until 100) {
54:         dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
55:         dut.clock.step()
56:       }
57: 
58:       // Verify RX FIFO status is non-empty
59:       val status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
60:       assert((status & 2) == 0, s"RX FIFO should not be empty, status=$status")
61: 
62:       // Check captured data
63:       val rxdata = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x0c.U)
64:       assert(rxdata == 0x55, s"Expected 0x55, got 0x${rxdata.toString(16)}")
65:     }
66:   }
67: 
68:   "SpiMaster DIV Timing" in {
69:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
70:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
71:       dut.clock.step()
72:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
73: 
74:       // Configure DIV=3: SCLK period = (DIV+1)*2 = 8 cycles
75:       // Standard Mode 0 (CPOL=0) results in sclk_reg=0 at idle
76:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x0301.U) // ENABLE=1, DIV=3, CPOL=0
77:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, 0xaa.U)
78: 
79:       // Wait for first edge (0 -> 1 for standard CPOL=0)
80:       while (dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue == 0) dut.clock.step()
81:       var steps = 0
82:       // Measure duration of '1' phase
83:       while (dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue == 1) {
84:         dut.clock.step()
85:         steps += 1
86:       }
87:       // Measure duration of '0' phase
88:       while (dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue == 0) {
89:         dut.clock.step()
90:         steps += 1
91:       }
92:       assert(steps == 8, s"Expected period 8, got $steps")
93:     }
94:   }
95: 
96:   "SpiMaster Manual CS" in {
97:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
98:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
99:       dut.clock.step()
100:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
101: 
102:       // Explicitly control CS line via CSID and CSMODE
103:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x14.U, 0x01.U) // CSMODE=Manual
104:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x10.U, 0x01.U) // CSID=0 active
105:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x01.U) // ENABLE=1
106: 
107:       dut.clock.step(10)
108:       assert(dut.io.spi.csb.peek().litValue == 0, "CS should stay asserted in manual mode")
109: 
110:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x10.U, 0x00.U) // Deassert
111:       dut.clock.step(10)
112:       assert(dut.io.spi.csb.peek().litValue == 1, "CS should stay deasserted in manual mode")
113:     }
114:   }
115: 
116:   "SpiMaster Top-level Async Clocks" in {
117:     val tlul_p = new TLULParameters(p)
118:     simulate(new Module {
119:       val io = IO(new Bundle {
120:         val tl         = Flipped(new OpenTitanTileLink.Host2Device(tlul_p))
121:         val spi        = new SpiIO
122:         val spi_clk_in = Input(Bool())
123:       })
124:       val dut = Module(new SpiMaster(p))
125:       dut.io.clk_i  := clock
126:       dut.io.rst_ni := (!reset.asBool).asAsyncReset
127:       dut.io.tl <> io.tl
128:       io.spi <> dut.io.spi
129:       dut.io.spi_clk_i := io.spi_clk_in.asClock
130:     }) { dut =>
131:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
132:       dut.clock.step()
133:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
134: 
135:       var spi_clk_val = false
136: 
137:       /** Helper to step both system bus and SPI clock domains.
138:         */
139:       def stepBoth(n: Int = 1): Unit = {
140:         for (_ <- 0 until n) {
141:           dut.clock.step()
142:           spi_clk_val = !spi_clk_val
143:           dut.io.spi_clk_in.poke(spi_clk_val.B)
144:         }
145:       }
146: 
147:       /** Specialized TileLink helper for CDC crossing test.
148:         */
149:       def tlWriteAsync(addr: UInt, data: UInt): Unit = {
150:         dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(true.B)
151:         dut.io.tl.a.bits.opcode.poke(TLULOpcodesA.PutFullData.asUInt)
152:         dut.io.tl.a.bits.address.poke(addr)
153:         dut.io.tl.a.bits.data.poke(data)
154:         dut.io.tl.a.bits.mask.poke(0xf.U)
155:         while (dut.io.tl.a.ready.peek().litValue == 0) stepBoth()
156:         stepBoth()
157:         dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(false.B)
158:         while (dut.io.tl.d.valid.peek().litValue == 0) stepBoth()
159:         dut.io.tl.d.ready.poke(true.B)
160:         stepBoth()
161:         dut.io.tl.d.ready.poke(false.B)
162:       }
163: 
164:       tlWriteAsync(0x04.U, 0x01.U) // Enable
165:       stepBoth(40)
166:       tlWriteAsync(0x08.U, 0x33.U) // Send byte
167: 
168:       var seen = 0
169:       for (_ <- 0 until 400) {
170:         stepBoth()
171:         if (dut.io.spi.csb.peek().litValue == 0) seen += 1
172:       }
173:       assert(seen > 0, "SPI logic did not activate across CDC bridge")
174:     }
175:   }
176: 
177:   "SpiMaster TX Backpressure" in {
178:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
179:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
180:       dut.clock.step()
181:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
182: 
183:       // Saturation test: fill FIFO and verify channel A stall
184:       for (i <- 0 until 4) {
185:         tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, i.U)
186:       }
187: 
188:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(true.B)
189:       dut.io.tl.a.bits.address.poke(0x08.U)
190:       dut.clock.step()
191:       assert(dut.io.tl.a.ready.peek().litValue == 0, "Host should be stalled when TX FIFO is full")
192:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(false.B)
193:     }
194:   }
195: 
196:   "SpiMaster RX Blocking Read" in {
197:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
198:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
199:       dut.clock.step()
200:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
201: 
202:       // Verification of atomic synchronization: reading from empty RXDATA stalls the bus
203:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(true.B)
204:       dut.io.tl.a.bits.address.poke(0x0c.U)
205:       dut.clock.step()
206:       assert(
207:         dut.io.tl.a.ready.peek().litValue == 0,
208:         "Host should be stalled when reading empty RX FIFO"
209:       )
210:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(false.B)
211:     }
212:   }
213: 
214:   "SpiMaster RX Overflow Stall" in {
215:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
216:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
217:       dut.clock.step()
218:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
219: 
220:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x0101.U) // Baud rate scaling
221: 
222:       // Saturate RX path
223:       for (i <- 0 until 4) {
224:         tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, (0xa0 + i).U)
225:         for (_ <- 0 until 100) {
226:           dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
227:           dut.clock.step()
228:         }
229:       }
230: 
231:       // 5th byte should hang until space is cleared
232:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, 0xee.U)
233:       for (_ <- 0 until 200) {
234:         dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
235:         dut.clock.step()
236:       }
237: 
238:       val sclk1 = dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue
239:       dut.clock.step(20)
240:       val sclk2 = dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue
241:       assert(sclk1 == sclk2, "SPI FSM should be stalled awaiting RX FIFO availability")
242: 
243:       // Clear space and verify resumption
244:       tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x0c.U)
245:       for (_ <- 0 until 100) {
246:         dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
247:         dut.clock.step()
248:       }
249:       val status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
250:       assert((status & 2) == 0, "Transaction should have finalized after FIFO read")
251:     }
252:   }
253: 
254:   "SpiMaster Invalid Address Access" in {
255:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
256:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
257:       dut.clock.step()
258:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
259: 
260:       // Get error on invalid address
261:       val (_, error) = tlRead(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x100.U)
262:       assert(error, "Invalid address access should return error")
263: 
264:       // Get error on write to read-only register
265:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(true.B)
266:       dut.io.tl.a.bits.opcode.poke(TLULOpcodesA.PutFullData.asUInt)
267:       dut.io.tl.a.bits.address.poke(0x00.U) // STATUS is RO
268:       dut.io.tl.a.bits.data.poke(1.U)
269:       while (dut.io.tl.a.ready.peek().litValue == 0) dut.clock.step()
270:       dut.clock.step()
271:       dut.io.tl.a.valid.poke(false.B)
272:       while (dut.io.tl.d.valid.peek().litValue == 0) dut.clock.step()
273:       assert(
274:         dut.io.tl.d.bits.error.peek().litValue != 0,
275:         "Write to RO register should return error"
276:       )
277:     }
278:   }
279: 
280:   "SpiMaster Mode 0 Sampling Verification" in {
281:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
282:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
283:       dut.clock.step()
284:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
285: 
286:       // Configure Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0)
287:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x01.U) // ENABLE=1, CPOL=0, CPHA=0
288:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, 0x88.U) // Send 10001000
289: 
290:       // Wait for bit shifting to start
291:       while (dut.io.spi.csb.peek().litValue == 1) dut.clock.step()
292: 
293:       // In Mode 0, data is driven by slave immediately on CS assertion.
294:       // Master must sample on the first available leading clock edge.
295:       for (_ <- 0 until 200) {
296:         // Simple loopback: MISO = MOSI
297:         dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
298:         dut.clock.step()
299:       }
300: 
301:       val rxdata = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x0c.U)
302:       assert(rxdata == 0x88, s"Expected 0x88, got 0x${rxdata.toString(16)}")
303:     }
304:   }
305: 
306:   "SpiMaster Multi-Mode Verification" in {
307:     // Test all 4 SPI modes (CPOL=0/1, CPHA=0/1)
308:     for (mode <- 0 until 4) {
309:       val cpol     = (mode >> 1) & 1
310:       val cpha     = mode & 1
311:       val ctrl_val = (cpol << 1) | (cpha << 2) | 1 // ENABLE=1
312: 
313:       simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
314:         dut.reset.poke(true.B)
315:         dut.clock.step()
316:         dut.reset.poke(false.B)
317: 
318:         tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, ctrl_val.U)
319:         tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, 0xa5.U)
320: 
321:         while (dut.io.spi.csb.peek().litValue == 1) dut.clock.step()
322: 
323:         // Wait enough time for the transfer to complete
324:         for (_ <- 0 until 500) {
325:           dut.io.spi.miso.poke(dut.io.spi.mosi.peek())
326:           dut.clock.step()
327:         }
328: 
329:         val rxdata = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x0c.U)
330:         assert(
331:           rxdata == 0xa5,
332:           s"Mode $mode (CPOL=$cpol, CPHA=$cpha) failed: expected 0xa5, got 0x${rxdata.toString(16)}"
333:         )
334:       }
335:     }
336:   }
337: 
338:   "SpiMaster Half-Duplex RX Mode" in {
339:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
340:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
341:       dut.clock.step()
342:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
343: 
344:       // Enable SPI with HDRX (bit 3)
345:       // Div=2, HDRX=1, Enable=1 -> 0x0209
346:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x0209.U)
347: 
348:       // In HDRX, SPI should start generating SCLK as long as RX FIFO is not full,
349:       // without needing a write to TXDATA.
350:       var sclk_edges = 0
351:       var last_sclk  = false
352:       for (_ <- 0 until 500) {
353:         val sclk = dut.io.spi.sclk.peek().litValue != 0
354:         if (sclk && !last_sclk) sclk_edges += 1
355:         last_sclk = sclk
356: 
357:         // Simple loopback: MISO = bit count (mocking some external data)
358:         dut.io.spi.miso.poke(true.B) // Just send all 1s for simplicity
359:         dut.clock.step()
360:       }
361: 
362:       assert(sclk_edges >= 8, "SCLK should have toggled in half-duplex mode")

365:       val status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
366:       assert((status & 2) == 0, "RX FIFO should have data")

369:       assert(rxdata == 0xff, s"Expected 0xFF from all-1s loopback, got 0x${rxdata.toString(16)}")
370:     }
371:   }

373:   "SpiMaster Half-Duplex TX Mode" in {
374:     simulate(new SpiMasterCtrl(p)) { dut =>
375:       dut.reset.poke(true.B)
376:       dut.clock.step()
377:       dut.reset.poke(false.B)
378: 
379:       // Enable SPI with HDTX (bit 4)
380:       // Div=2, HDTX=1, Enable=1 -> 0x0211
381:       tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x04.U, 0x0211.U)
382: 
383:       // Write 8 bytes to TXDATA. With an RX FIFO of size 4, this would
384:       // normally stall if RX wasn't being drained. In HDTX mode, it should
385:       // proceed without stalls and without filling the RX FIFO.
386:       for (i <- 0 until 8) {
387:         tlWrite(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x08.U, i.U)
388:         // Wait for byte to finish (busy bit in status)
389:         var status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
390:         while ((status & 1) != 0) {
391:           dut.clock.step()
392:           status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
393:         }
394:       }
395: 
396:       // Check that RX FIFO is still empty
397:       val status = tlReadData(dut.io.tl, dut.clock, 0x00.U)
398:       assert((status & 2) != 0, "RX FIFO should be empty in HDTX mode")
399:     }
400:   }
401: }

98:       ((if (srcFixed) 1L else 0L) << 27) |
99:       ((if (dstFixed) 1L else 0L) << 28) |

109:   /** Reactive memory model: step clock while servicing host port transactions. Runs for `maxCycles`
110:     * or until DMA is no longer busy.
111:     *
112:     * Timing: In Chisel sim, poke is combinational (immediate), step advances the clock. We keep
113:     * a.ready=1. When a.valid is seen (peek), that means on the NEXT step, fire will occur. We
114:     * capture the request, step (fire happens, DMA transitions), then present D response, step again
115:     * (D fire happens).
116:     */
117:   def runDmaWithMemory(
118:       dut: DmaEngine,
119:       mem: scala.collection.mutable.Map[Long, Byte],
120:       maxCycles: Int = 2000
121:   ): Int = {
122:     val host     = dut.io.tl_host
123:     var txnCount = 0
124: 
125:     for (cycle <- 0 until maxCycles) {
126:       // Default: ready to accept A, no D response
127:       host.a.ready.poke(true.B)
128:       host.d.valid.poke(false.B)
129: 
130:       // Check if DMA is presenting an A channel request
131:       if (host.a.valid.peek().litValue != 0) {
132:         // Capture request details (they're combinationally valid now)
133:         val opcode  = host.a.bits.opcode.peek().litValue.toInt
134:         val address = host.a.bits.address.peek().litValue.toLong
135:         val size    = host.a.bits.size.peek().litValue.toInt
136:         val nbytes  = 1 << size
137:         val wdata   = host.a.bits.data.peek().litValue
138: 
139:         // Step: a.fire occurs (valid=1, ready=1 on this edge)
140:         dut.clock.step()
141: 
142:         // Now DMA has moved to response-wait state.
143:         // Present D channel response.
144:         host.a.ready.poke(false.B)
145:         host.d.valid.poke(true.B)
146:         host.d.bits.source.poke(0.U)
147:         host.d.bits.error.poke(false.B)
148:         host.d.bits.sink.poke(0.U)
149:         host.d.bits.param.poke(0.U)
150:         host.d.bits.size.poke(size.U)
151: 
152:         if (opcode == 4) {
153:           // Get: read from mem, place data at correct byte lane per TL-UL spec
154:           var rdata      = BigInt(0)
155:           val busBytes   = 16 // 128-bit bus
156:           val byteOffset = (address % busBytes).toInt
157:           for (i <- 0 until nbytes) {
158:             val b = mem.getOrElse(address + i, 0.toByte) & 0xff
159:             rdata = rdata | (BigInt(b) << ((byteOffset + i) * 8))
160:           }
161:           host.d.bits.opcode.poke(1.U) // AccessAckData
162:           host.d.bits.data.poke(rdata.U)
163:         } else {
164:           // PutFullData: write to mem, extract data from correct byte lane
165:           val busBytes   = 16 // 128-bit bus
166:           val byteOffset = (address % busBytes).toInt
167:           for (i <- 0 until nbytes) {
168:             mem(address + i) = ((wdata >> ((byteOffset + i) * 8)) & 0xff).toByte
169:           }
170:           host.d.bits.opcode.poke(0.U) // AccessAck
171:           host.d.bits.data.poke(0.U)
172:         }
173: 
174:         // Wait for D to be accepted
175:         var dWait = 0
176:         while (host.d.ready.peek().litValue == 0 && dWait < 100) {
177:           dut.clock.step()
178:           dWait += 1
179:         }
180:         // Step: d.fire occurs
181:         dut.clock.step()
182:         host.d.valid.poke(false.B)
183:         txnCount += 1
184:       } else {
185:         dut.clock.step()
186:       }
187:     }
188:     txnCount
189:   }
